`yes`: output a line again and again.

## Synopsis

<strong>yes</strong> \[<em>string</em>...\]

## Description

<strong>yes</strong> writes its arguments, joined by spaces, as a line, again and again, until a write fails (for instance when the reader of its pipe is gone, which also sends it SIGPIPE). With no arguments the line is <strong>y</strong>.

Lines are written many at a time, about 4096 bytes in each write, as GNU yes does.

## Exit status

1 when a write fails (it never ends on its own).

## Examples

```text
yes | head -n 3
yes no | head -n 2
```

## See also

<strong>head</strong>(1), <strong>sh</strong>(1)
